title: ENDEX: Lily Home, Alert Cancelled, 18:05

fields.resolution: ENDEX. It is 18:05 on Saturday, four hours and five minutes after the first 911 call, and Lily Ashby is safe and back with her family, who heard the news from the Victim and Family Liaison before anyone else. OSP Northern Communications cancelled the alert at the Incident Commander's request and cleared the LEDS/NCIC missing-person record by phone after a logged read-back from Console 2. The joint closing statement has gone out with one set of facts, Search and Rescue is checked out, and the investigation continues under written custody transfers. This ends the exercise.
finalState: Lily Ashby is safe and with her family. The family was told first, in person, by the Liaison.
The alert is cancelled by OSP at the IC's request. The LEDS/NCIC record is cleared by phone, with the read-back and time logged.
All 22 Search and Rescue volunteers are checked out at the Fire District 1 check-in point. Deschutes County deputies are released from the gates.
One joint closing statement has gone out from the Sheriff's Office, APD, OSP and Fire District 1, with matching times and place and no word on the child's condition or the person in custody.
CAD 26-081377 stays open for Investigations. The person, the pickup and the Highway 26 scene are under written custody transfers.
fields.hotWashTransition: Thank you, everyone. Lily is home, so put down the phones and radios and stop play now. Before you leave your seat, hand in your logs, worksheets and forms. We'll take ten minutes and then start the hot wash here in the room.
fields.hotWashMethod: Timeline walk-back, then 3-Up, 3-Down: each role puts its key decision times on the wall chronology against the plan targets, then names three things that worked and three that broke.
hotWashQuestions: When was unified command formed and written on the briefing sheet, compared with the 30-minute target after Wren 14 arrived at 14:10? Who was on the sheet, and were the objectives reviewed every 60 minutes?

Walk through the AMBER worksheet. At each 30-minute review, which criterion was met or not met, and why? What finally gave us one vehicle description to stand behind, and what did the 16:07 decision cost or gain against the one-hour target?

Did every agency's public text carry the same times, place and vehicle? How fast did we correct the 'black Dodge', 'found at the food booths' and named-man posts, and did we ever describe a suspect or tactics?
When the LEDS terminal went down at 17:25, did the paper chronology keep the original times, and did the phone clearance with OSP follow a proper read-back?
Did the family hear every major development from the Liaison before the public or the press did? What would have kept them out of the hallway, away from the radio and the KWRN camera?
fields.facilitatorNote: Before the break, collect: the CAD 26-081377 chronology; the paper chronology from the LEDS outage with its original handwritten times; the AMBER worksheet with every 30-minute review; all unified command briefing sheets; the PIO release log and rumor-monitoring sheet; and the custody transfer forms for the person, the pickup and the scene. Remind the room that today's discussion is the quick debrief. Under the plan, the Undersheriff runs the formal hot wash within 7 days and the HSEEP after-action report within 30 days.
